rfi.title: Lebanon war reopens old divisions as fears grow for country's unity
rfi.description: Israel's war in southern Lebanon is reopening old wounds far beyond the battlefield. More than a million people have been displaced since Israel and Hezbollah returned to full-scale conflict in March, while political leaders remain split over the powerful Shiite movement and negotiations with Israel. As calls for federalism and even partition become louder, the war is reviving debate over Lebanon's political system, national identity and territorial unity.

The vote marks a significant moment in a decades-long fight over chlordecone, a toxic chemical that continued to be used in the French Caribbean after it was banned in mainland France.

Meanwhile, the question of EU enlargement is also on the cards at a Western Balkans summit.

france24fr.description: Une vidéo montrant des centaines de migrants franchissant une clôture à la frontière espagnole, datée au 30 mai 2026, est devenue virale. Sur X, des internautes, Elon Musk en tête, demandent à Grok, l’IA de la plateforme, de la vérifier. Mais le chatbot confirme à tort sa date : ces images, sorties de leur contexte, datent en réalité de 2022.

france24fr.title: Pêche au calmar: enquête sur une destruction de grande ampleur
france24fr.description: Un scandale environnemental et humain de grande ampleur. L'ONG Environmental Justice Foundation (EJS) a publié une enquête sur la pêche au calmar. Elle a recueilli le témoignage de plus 400 marins victimes de travail forcé et de violences sur des bateaux, principalement chinois, en haute mer. Ils décrivent une pêche destructrice qui décime les populations de calmars avec des effets dévastateurs sur tout l'écosystème mais aussi des pêches illégales et barbares de dauphins, requins, phoques, etc.

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : le récit d'une semaine d’angoisse et de révélations autour du principal suspect
france24fr.description: Alors que Lyhanna, 11 ans, est portée disparue depuis six jours dans le sud-ouest de la France, un corps a été découvert jeudi à proximité du lieu où la collégienne a été vue pour la dernière fois. Depuis sa disparition, l'enquête a mis au jour plusieurs plaintes et signalements visant le principal suspect, une connaissance de la famille.

france24fr.title: "Flamants roses" contre famille Trump : la contestation qui fait vaciller le gouvernement albanais
france24fr.description: Un projet de tourisme de luxe sur une île d’Albanie, porté par Jared Kushner et Ivanka Trump, a été l’étincelle qui a provoqué des manifestations inédites à Tirana. Ce mouvement, qui a reçu le surnom de "révolution des flamants roses", traduit une remise en question plus profonde du système politique albanais.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : l'opposant Rached Ghannouchi condamné à la prison à vie pour terrorisme
france24fr.description: En Tunisie, 35 personnes ont été condamnées à des peines allant de dix ans de prison à la perpétuité, pour constitution et participation à une organisation terroriste concernant les assassinats politiques de 2013 de deux figures de la gauche Chokri Belaïd et Mohamed Brahmi. france24fr.title: "Je crains une vraie violence" : Donald Trump va-t-il rejeter les résultats des midterms ?
france24fr.description: Aux États-Unis, la date des élections de mi-mandats approche. Plusieurs sondages publiés ces dernières semaines montrent que la popularité de Donald Trump est plus basse qu'elle n'a jamais été dans le pays. Mais quelle sera la réaction du président si les démocrates l'emportent ? La juriste et américaniste Anne Deysine livre son analyse à France 24 dans le podcast Avec Judith. Retrouvez l'épisode en intégralité sur la chaîne YouTube de France 24.

france24fr.title: Décès de Marjane Satrapi : comment "Persepolis" a changé le regard sur l’Iran ?
france24fr.description: Marjane Satrapi, artiste franco-iranienne mondialement connue pour sa bande dessinée Persepolis, est décédée à l’âge de 56 ans. Invitée sur France 24, la romancière franco-iranienne Sorour Kasmaï, qui était l’une de ses proches, est revenue sur l’héritage de son amie. Selon elle, le regard à la fois accessible et percutant porté par Persepolis sur l’Iran des mollahs a contribué à faire évoluer l’image des Iraniens en France. france24fr.description: La Chambre américaine des représentants a adopté mercredi un texte ordonnant le retrait des troupes américaines dans la guerre contre l'Iran, un camouflet pour Donald Trump qui a engagé les Etats-Unis dans ce conflit le 28 février. Le président américain a laissé entendre que cette initiative "antipatriotique" perturbait les négociations avec Téhéran. Les explications de Matthieu Mabin depuis Washington.

france24fr.title: Débarquement : 82 ans après, les derniers vétérans américains en Normandie
france24fr.description: En Normandie, les commémorations du Débarquement du 6 juin 1944 réunissent cette année les derniers vétérans américains, tous centenaires, revenus sur les plages 82 ans après les combats. france24fr.title: RD Congo : une journée "ville morte" à Kinshasa
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, la capitale a tourné au ralenti ce mercredi. À l’appel de la plateforme d’opposition C64, de nombreux habitants de Kinshasa étaient invités à observer une journée "ville morte" pour s’opposer à la volonté de la majorité au pouvoir de modifier la Constitution. Les explications avec notre correspondante à Kinshasa, Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Pour Emmanuel Macron, l'éditorialiste Xenia Fedorova sert la "propagande d'État" russe
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron a estimé jeudi que Xenia Fedorova, ancienne directrice générale de la chaine Russia Today en langue française, était au service de la "propagande d'État" russe. france24fr.description: Dans un Moyen-Orient marqué par les conflits, la réhabilitation des écoles est devenue un enjeu crucial. À Gaza, les familles cherchent à préserver l’accès à l’éducation pour éviter qu’une génération entière ne soit privée d’avenir malgré les traumatismes de la guerre. france24fr.description: Le scientifique Svante Arrhenius est le premier à avoir fait le lien entre réchauffement du climat, émissions de CO₂ et énergies fossiles. Et tout ça, dès 1896.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le football, une religion au Mexique
france24fr.description: Pour le coup d’envoi de la Coupedu monde le 11 juin, le Mexique jouera le premier match au stade de la capitale. Historiquement, l'équipe nationale du pays n’a jamais brillé par ses exploits sportifs et est arrivée jusqu’en quart de finale en 1970 et 1986. observador.description: O Ministério Público alemão pediu prisão perpétua para o psiquiatra saudita que atropelou multidão no mercado de Natal de Magdeburgo, matando seis pessoas e ferindo mais de 300 em dezembro de 2024.

observador.title: "Somos candidatos sim, favorito é quem já ganhou o Mundial"
observador.description: José Sá destacou a experiência que existe em todos os jogadores na Seleção portuguesa e reforçou o estatuto de candidato da equipa das quinas. Guarda-redes descarta favoritismo.

observador.title: Guiné-Bissau: Líder da oposição em prisão domiciliária
observador.description: O líder da oposição guineense, Domingos Simões Pereira, regressou a prisão domiciliária sem novas medidas de coação. É suspeito numa alegada tentativa de golpe de Estado.

observador.title: American Airlines suspende rotas devido a combustíveis
observador.description: A American Airlines suspendeu temporariamente algumas rotas em agosto e setembro, devido ao custo dos combustíveis. Passageiros afetados receberão alternativas de viagem ou reembolsos.

observador.title: 18h. José Sá diz que Portugal é um dos candidatos à vitória
observador.description: O guarda redes da Seleção Nacional foi hoje o porta voz da equipa e diz que Portugal não sendo favorito é um dos candidatos à vitória no Campeonato do Mundo.

observador.title: Isabel dos Santos: "A verdade vem finalmente ao de cima"
observador.description: Empresária e filha do antigo Presidente angolano reagiu a decisão que confirma que agiu de boa fé e sem abuso de direito. A conclusão é diferente da "narrativa política" que foi apresentada.

observador.title: Avião perde o trem de aterragem e funcionários ficam feridos
observador.description: Parte dianteira da aeronave que estava a ser preparada para descolar para os Estados Unidos cedeu na pista do aeroporto de Frankfurt, na Alemanha. Lufthansa não divulga número de feridos.

observador.title: HSBC acusado de ajudar a desviar fundos
observador.description: A subsidiária suíça do banco HSBC foi formalmente acusada de ter ajudado o ex-governador do Banco Central do Líbano, Riad Salamé, a desviar fundos.

observador.title: Montenegro: recorreu ao TC mas nega "novos recursos"
observador.description: Tribunal Constitucional registou entrada de recursos interpostos em 2025 e 2026 pelo primeiro-ministro "de decisões proferidas pela Entidade para a Transparência".

observador.title: IL acusa PCP e CGTP de "tónica agressiva" sobre greve geral
observador.description: A líder da Iniciativa Liberal acusa a CGTP e o PCP de terem adotado "uma tónica agressiva, de completa inflexibilidade" em relação à reforma laboral.

observador.title: Retrospetiva. No teatro de opulência de Gianni Versace
observador.description: O museu Maillol, em Paris, recebe a primeiro grande mostra francesa dedicada ao criador desde 1986. De esboços a silhuetas originais, de Naomi a Diana, o barroco de Gianni revela-se em 450 peças.

observador.title: Harry e Meghan celebram os 5 anos da princesa Lilibet
observador.description: "A menina dos nossos sonhos. Feliz quinto aniversário, Lili", escreveu a duquesa de Sussex na legenda das duas imagens publicadas no Instagram, que mostram a princesa entre os pais, Meghan e Harry.

observador.title: A história do americano condenado por espiar para Israel
observador.description: Há 40 anos, Jonathan Pollard confessou ter vendido documentos dos EUA a Israel e foi condenado a perpétua. Netanyahu desdobrou-se em esforços para o tirar da prisão, mas agora é criticado pelo espião.

observador.title: 17h. Benfica já informou CMVM sobre interesse em Mourinho
observador.description: O Benfica já comunicou à CMVM o interesse que Florentino Pérez e o Real Madrid têm no treinador encarnado e quais os valores de uma futura transferência.

observador.title: Benfica confirma que Mourinho sai se Florentino Pérez vencer
observador.description: O Benfica informou o mercado que recebeu da parte da candidatura de Florentino Pérez a "firme intenção" de contratar José Mourinho, caso vença as eleições de domingo no Real Madrid.

observador.title: Seguro e Montenegro comemoram juntos o Dia de Portugal
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro e o Presidente da República encontram-se no sábado no Luxemburgo, onde decorrem as celebrações fora do país. Ilha Terceira também recebe comemorações.

observador.title: Antiga enfermeira acusa amigo da família de violação
observador.description: Joey Mawson, piloto amigo do filho de Schumacher, foi a tribunal por alegadamente ter violado uma enfermeira da equipa médica do antigo piloto. Factos remontam a 2019 e a queixa a 2022.

observador.title: 16h. Preço gasóleo deverá subir para a semana
observador.description: São previsões e ainda podem mudar até ao fecho dos mercados amanhã. Ainda, o homem que fugiu do Tribunal de Ponte de Sor está indiciado por 20 crimes.

spiegel.title: Kroatien: Vier Tote bei Absturz von Kleinflugzeug
spiegel.description: Ein in Deutschland registriertes Kleinflugzeug ist über der kroatischen Halbinsel Istrien verunglückt. Es gibt keine überlebenden Insassen. Die Unfallursache wird noch ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Pflegereform: Nina Warken spart bei den Falschen - Kommentar
spiegel.description: Pflegende Angehörige entlasten den Staat um Milliarden. Doch ihre Rentenansprüche wird die Pflegeversicherung künftig nicht mehr zahlen. Damit steigt das Armutsrisiko, vor allem für Frauen.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Gericht verurteilt Mann nach Schüssen in Hamburg zu langer Haftstrafe
spiegel.description: Wegen eines Kiosks und unbezahlter Steuern eskalierte ein Streit in Hamburg-Billstedt. Ein Mensch starb. Das Landgericht hat den Schützen zu zehneinhalb Jahren Gefängnis verurteilt.

spiegel.title: Insel Ostervilm: So lief die Versteigerung der ehemaligen DDR-Militärstation vor Rügen
spiegel.description: Die Versteigerung einer Insel vor Rügen erregte bundesweite Aufmerksamkeit. Den Zuschlag bekam ein Mann, der die heruntergekommene Militärstation darauf noch nie gesehen hat. Was er mit dem künstlichen Eiland vorhat.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Fußball-WM, Donald Trump, Wladimir Putin, Russland, Google, Stechmücken
spiegel.description: Donald Trump dürfte die Fußball-WM prägen. Russische Experten äußern erstmals laut Zweifel an Putins Ukrainekrieg. Und Google will Mücken mit Mücken bekämpfen. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: KNDS: Prüfer sehen Anhaltspunkte für Unregelmäßigkeiten bei Panzerhersteller
spiegel.description: Der Panzerbauer KNDS beauftragte nach SPIEGEL-Enthüllungen über dubiose Provisionszahlungen externe Prüfer. Die sind nun fündig geworden. Das Unternehmen kündigt personelle Konsequenzen an.

spiegel.title: »Rote Kobolde« über Tibet: Spektakuläre Aufnahmen seltener roter Blitze
spiegel.description: Sie sind ebenso rar wie spektakulär: Einem chinesischen Fotografen sind Aufnahmen von roten Blitzen über Tibet gelungen. Sehen Sie im Video, was sie ausmacht.

spiegel.title: Vechta: Betrüger verschafft sich 120.000 Eier und wird zu zwei Jahren Haft verurteilt
spiegel.description: Ein 45-Jähriger holte über zwei Jahre lang regelmäßig Eier von einer Legehennenfarm ab – mit einer simplen Lüge. Erst als eine Urlaubsvertretung misstrauisch wurde, flog der Schwindel auf.

spiegel.title: AfD: Was sich die Partei von ihrer Russland-Mission verspricht
spiegel.description: Europa will Russland isolieren, eine AfD-Delegation reist stattdessen nach Sankt Petersburg und trifft Putins Vertraute. Was sich die Rechtsextremen von dem Trip versprechen und worauf der Kreml setzt.

spiegel.title: FC St. Pauli trennt sich von Trainer Alexander Blessin
spiegel.description: Zwei Jahre lang trainierte Alexander Blessin den FC St. Pauli. Zuerst sah es aus, als wollte der Club trotz des Abstiegs mit ihm weitermachen. Jetzt soll es doch mit einem neuen Coach in die zweite Liga gehen.

spiegel.title: Buckelwal »Timmy«: »Bild« macht eine Wal-Obduktion zum KI-Tatort
spiegel.description: Der verendete Wal aus der Ostsee kommt unters Messer, sehr viele Medien berichten vorab. Auch die »Bild«-Zeitung beteiligt sich und lässt sich die passenden Bilder kurzerhand dazuerfinden.

spiegel.title: Wal »Timmy«: Obduktion des angespülten Buckelwals vor Anholt gestartet
spiegel.description: Vor rund drei Wochen wurde der Kadaver des mehrfach in der Ostsee gestrandeten Wals vor der dänischen Insel Anholt angespült. Nun hat die Untersuchung begonnen.

spiegel.title: Axel Schreiber ist tot: »Türkisch für Anfänger«-Schauspieler wurde 49 Jahre alt
spiegel.description: »Axel« war sein Rollenname in der Comedyserie »Türkisch für Anfänger«, die Axel Schreiber 2006 bekannt machte. Es folgten zahlreiche Auftritte in TV-Produktionen. Nun ist der Schauspieler gestorben, er wurde 49 Jahre alt.

spiegel.title: Fußball-Fanhilfen kritisieren neue Stadionverbotsrichtlinien des DFB
spiegel.description: DFB und DFL haben eine neue Instanz geschaffen: Die »ZAÜS« soll in Zukunft die Stadionverbotskommissionen der Vereine überwachen und auch selbst entscheiden können. Fanvertreter kritisieren das Vorgehen.

spiegel.title: Pflegereform: Grüne und Linke warnen vor schweren Belastungen für Bürger
spiegel.description: Lange wurde er erwartet, nun liegt der Entwurf der Pflegereform von Gesundheitsministerin Warken vor. Grüne und Linke kritisieren die Ideen scharf. Auch in den Regierungsfraktionen sind nicht alle begeistert.

spiegel.title: Abstimmung in der Uno verloren: Fährt Deutschland jetzt seine Zahlungen zurück?
spiegel.description: Deutschland hat in den kommenden zwei Jahren keinen Sitz im Uno-Sicherheitsrat. Warum das eine herbe Niederlage für Außenminister Wadephul und Kanzler Merz ist. Und welche Konsequenzen drohen.

spiegel.title: Metallica: Fast 10.000 Blutspender in Deutschland dank »Bleeding Me«-Aktion
spiegel.description: »Bleeding Me« ist ein Song von Metallica, aber auch das Motto einer Aktion der Band zusammen mit dem Deutschen Roten Kreuz. Tausende Fans machten mit, für ein kleines Geschenk.

spiegel.title: Commerzbank-Übernahme durch UniCredit: Deutsche wittern falsches Spiel
spiegel.description: Italiens Großbank UniCredit will Deutschlands zweitgrößtes Geldhaus schlucken, die Übernahmeschlacht wird immer schmutziger. Jetzt wittern die Deutschen falsches Spiel der Italiener – und rufen die Finanzaufsicht um Hilfe.

elpais.title: La UCO pide al juez que recabe todos los movimientos bancarios del PSOE en 2024 y 2025 y datos a Hacienda del Partido Socialista y el PSC
elpais.description: La Guardia Civil solicita a Pedraz que varias empresas implicadas en la trama del ‘caso Leire’ remitan “las relaciones comerciales” que mantuvieron con ambos partidos

elpais.title: Los audios del ‘caso Leire Díez’: “Mi siguiente conversación va a ser con la directora de la Guardia Civil [...] es de mi confianza”
elpais.description: EL PAÍS accede a las grabaciones del sumario judicial, que expone que la exmilitante socialista se reunió al menos tres veces con la directora del instituto armado

elpais.title: La UCO registra la sede de Tubos Reunidos por una pieza secreta del ‘caso Leire’
elpais.description: El juez ordena la medida tras un informe de la Guardia Civil que apunta a nuevos implicados en las supuestas irregularidades en la concesión de una millonaria ayuda pública

elpais.title: David Sánchez niega haber hecho valer su apellido: “No tengo capacidad de influir en nada”
elpais.description: El hermano del presidente califica de “malentendido” el mensaje que intercambió con un amigo sobre la adjudicación a este de un puesto en la Diputación de Badajoz

elpais.title: Ayuso, a horas de la llegada del Papa a Madrid, sobre la regularización de migrantes: “Es importar pobreza masiva”
elpais.description: La presidenta pregunta a los partidos de izquierda si ahora se han vuelto “capillitas”

elpais.title: El consejero de Cultura de Ayuso se ríe del calor que pasan los niños en el colegio: “Es fuente de inspiración”
elpais.description: La oposición ha debatido este jueves en la Asamblea de Madrid sobre la falta de climatización de las aulas de los colegios madrileños, a lo que Mariano de Paco ha respondido que “cuando hace calor, hace calor”

elpais.title: Todos los cortes de tráfico de Madrid y Barcelona, calles a evitar y restricciones a la movilidad por la visita del Papa en España
elpais.description: Los actos y los desplazamientos en papamóvil de León XIV entre el 6 y el 12 de junio provocará cortes de calles, desvíos y alteraciones en el transporte público

elpais.title: Muere la historietista y cineasta Marjane Satrapi, autora de ‘Persépolis’, a los 56 años
elpais.description: La familia de la dibujante francoiraní de cómics informa de que ha fallecido “de tristeza” tras la muerte de su marido hace un año

elpais.title: Marjane Satrapi: directa, cortante, transparente, desbordante, genial
elpais.description: Así era, idéntica a sí misma, a la niña de ‘Persépolis’, la Mafalda persa, uno de esos milagros literarios que explican todo un mundo, el de quien creció durante la revolución y los primeros años del odio de los ayatolás

elpais.title: Hacienda promete acordar los Presupuestos de 2027 con los socios antes de presentarlos al Congreso
elpais.description: Arcadi España pide a las comunidades del PP que acudan a las reuniones bilaterales para negociar el modelo de financiación

elpais.title: Ignacio Dancausa, el joven apadrinado de Ayuso, se hace con la presidencia de Nuevas Generaciones del PP
elpais.description: Los dos candidatos que habían logrado los avales necesarios han acordado una lista de unidad para el congreso de julio

elpais.title: La UE se prepara para abrir las negociaciones de adhesión de Ucrania tras el levantamiento del veto húngaro
elpais.description: Budapest y Kiev encauzan su relación y dejan atrás el enfrentamiento que se produjo entre los dos países durante la era Orbán

elpais.title: El exasesor de Trump John Bolton se declarará culpable de manejo indebido de documentos clasificados
elpais.description: El antiguo consejero de Seguridad Nacional se enfrenta a 18 cargos de tenencia indebida y transmisión de información que afectaba a la defensa nacional

elpais.title: Israel prosigue los bombardeos en Líbano pese a la prórroga del alto el fuego: “Tenemos libertad de acción”
elpais.description: Hezbolá lanza drones contra las localidades fronterizas y rechaza la tregua porque es parcial y mantiene las tropas israelíes en el país

elpais.title: Petro cede y descarta la idea de convocar una Constituyente
elpais.description: El comité que promovía la reforma a la Constitución de 1991, un proyecto que había despertado críticas y temores, da a conocer la decisión, que reformula el panorama electoral a dos semanas de la segunda vuelta

elpais.title: El 65% de profesores catalanes votan no al pacto educativo y anuncian nuevas huelgas la próxima semana
elpais.description: Educación anuncia que aplicará el nuevo acuerdo, después de que Profesores de Secundaria anuncie que lo firmará

elpais.title: Un atasco en la A-6 desata el caos en la prueba de acceso a la universidad: los campus de Madrid cambian los horarios
elpais.description: El incidente lleva a la comisión organizadora de los exámenes a adoptar medidas excepcionales

elpais.title: El primer positivo español por hantavirus supera la enfermedad y es dado de alta
elpais.description: El segundo caso presenta febrícula y el resto de los aislados en el Gómez Ulla podrán salir este fin de semana si dan negativo en una PCR

nyt.title: John Bolton, Ex-Trump Adviser, Reaches Deal to Plead Guilty Over Classified Information
nyt.description: The former Trump national security adviser plans to plead guilty to a count of illegal retention of classified information, which could result in a fine and possibly prison time of up to five years.

nyt.title: Trump’s Arch Project to Face Questions and Criticism at Planning Meeting
nyt.description: The National Capital Planning Commission received nearly 1,700 comments about President Trump’s plans to build a 250-foot arch in the nation’s capital. Almost all opposed the idea.

nyt.title: Trump Says He Plans to Nominate Blanche for Attorney General
nyt.description: Todd Blanche has been serving as the acting attorney general. A formal nomination to the post would be the president’s latest move to place loyalists in top government jobs.

nyt.title: Justice Department Tells Prosecutors to Pursue Immigrant Vote Fraud Cases
nyt.description: About 90 such investigations are currently open, a Justice Department official told prosecutors. The tally offers a glimpse inside the scale of the administration’s efforts.

nyt.title: American Farms Rely More Than Ever on the Troubled H-2A Visa Program
nyt.description: The Trump administration is allowing in more agricultural guest workers under the H-2A program, but preventing abuses is proving difficult.

nyt.title: Early Research Suggests a Path to Predict and Prevent Lung Cancer
nyt.description: Scientists have identified proteins that could signal increased lung cancer risk, as well as a drug that could reduce the odds of a tumor developing.

nyt.title: Ultra-Orthodox Riot Shocks Israelis In Latest Protest At Military Draft
nyt.description: Israel’s Haredim have escalated their protests against military service in recent weeks, underscoring growing divisions ahead of national elections.

nyt.title: Hezbollah’s Fiber-Optic Drones Expose Cracks in Israeli Defenses
nyt.description: The Lebanese militant group’s attacks have caught Israelis off guard, forcing its political and military leaders to scramble for solutions.

nyt.title: Netflix’s New Movie Strategy: Fewer, Better Films
nyt.description: Dan Lin doesn’t fawn over stars or write blank checks. And he still greenlights more movies than anyone.

nyt.title: ‘Teachers Are Going to Hate It’: How Social Media Apps Hooked Teens at School
nyt.description: Internal documents show how tech giants grabbed children’s attention throughout the day, a strategy that schools say has undermined education.

nyt.title: Gwynne Shotwell, Elon Musk’s No. 2 at SpaceX, Is the Company’s Steady Hand
nyt.description: Gwynne Shotwell, the president and chief operating officer, is the adult-in-the-room foil to Mr. Musk as SpaceX prepares for a blockbuster initial public offering.

nyt.title: Who’s Excited for SpaceX’s I.P.O.? Space Nerds.
nyt.description: Few are as delighted by the pending market debut as the vibrant community of space enthusiasts who want to push discovery of the final frontier.

nyt.title: Marjane Satrapi, the Author of ‘Persepolis,’ Dies at 56
nyt.description: Her popular graphic novel series, published in the early 2000s, followed an Iranian girl through the Islamic Revolution and the Iran-Iraq War.

nyt.title: Review: ‘Persepolis,’ by Marjane Satrapi
nyt.description: A memoir and a history of Iran’s turbulent 20th-century politics, one comic strip frame at a time.

nyt.title: Bill Bradley, 2-Time Champion With the Knicks, Cheers on His Old Team in the Finals
nyt.description: Watching Game 1 of the Knicks-Spurs series, Bill Bradley, the two-time N.B.A. champion and former U.S. senator, spoke reverently of teamwork — and had a few choice words for the refs.

nyt.title: Priest’s Ebola Death Stirs Fear and Doubt in Congolese Town
nyt.description: Priest’s Ebola Death Stirs Fear an Doubt in Congolese Town

nyt.title: Why Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass Has to Fight for Her Job
nyt.description: Ms. Bass, a Democrat, has had a roller-coaster first term. She now faces the first runoff since 2005 for an incumbent mayor in the city.

nyt.title: The Democrats’ Big Decision: Black Representation or More Blue Seats?
nyt.description: As Republicans break up majority-Black House districts, Democrats must decide whether to preserve seats concentrated in urban areas or push them into white suburbs to target G.O.P. seats.

republika.description: Parla Roberto Gagnor, sceneggiatore e storico collaboratore del settimanale: “Non mi pento di quello che ho scritto”

republika.title: Inghilterra, marea di tweet di Musk dopo il 18enne bianco ucciso. Starmer: “Vuole spaccare il Paese”
republika.description: Come due anni fa, il miliardario soffia sul fuoco delle tensioni: quasi 150 post online contro migranti, media e società britannica nelle ultime ore. La furia del primo ministro

republika.title: Tutti i generi della risata: viaggio nella comicità Lgbtq+
republika.description: Non è solo un (seguitissimo) fenomeno social. I comici queer hanno successo in teatro e in tv ben oltre i confini della comunità. Senza rinunciare a battute politiche scorrette. Qualcuno si offende? Peggio per loro

republika.description: I cabaret berlinesi e le commedie di Oscar Wilde. Le raffinatezze di Paolo Poli e le parolacce di Tondelli. Come l’ironia ha contribuito a plasmare un’identità

republika.title: Speciale Festival: A Verona debutta la Traviata di Paul Curran
republika.description: Intervista al regista scozzese, che all’Arena sposta l’opera di Verdi all’inizio del XX secolo. Fra toreri e un elefante enorme. E sul Venerdì in edicola il 5 giugno 28 pagine con il meglio di teatro, musica, opera e danza dell’estate.

republika.title: Tienanmen, 37 anni dopo. Rubio ricorda le vittime del massacro. L’ira di Pechino: “Diffamazione”
republika.description: Il segretario di Stato Usa marca l’anniversario della repressione: “Nessuna censura può cancellare il passato”. Nella capitale cinese attivisti allontanati. Palloncini e fili rossi a Hong Kong: i gesti di artisti che provano ad aggirare i divieti in nome della memoria

Violenze sessuali alla Scuola militare Teulié, arrestato un commissario: abusi per superare esami
republika.description: Le accuse sono di concussione, violenza sessuale e maltrattamenti

republika.title: Giorgetti: “Calma sulla flessibilità, non possiamo sbagliare”. Accise, sconti prorogati dopo il 6
republika.description: Il ministro dell’Economia invita alla cautela: “Lo spazio non è esagerato”. La proroga del taglio delle accise con un decreto ministeriale

republika.description: La coppia azzurra si impone al super tie-break sulla canadese Gabriela Dabrowski e lo statunitense Evan King

republika.description: Il procuratore capo di Roma Francesco Lo Voi torna sulla richiesta di acquisire le conversazioni tra il deputato di Fratelli d’Italia e Mauro Caroccia, prestanome del clan Senese. “Delmastro non è indagato”, precisa, ma i pm vogliono verificare i rapporti tra i soci della Bisteccheria d’Italia

republika.description: Sono 4,9 milioni i cittadini che per recarsi alle urne devono percorrere decine, centinaia o migliaia di chilometri perché vivono lontano dal luogo di residenza

npr.title: North Korea unveils a new plant to produce fuel for nuclear weapons
npr.description: State media photos on the place showed it is likely a plant to produce weapons-grade uranium.

npr.title: Israel and Lebanon reach an agreement, but ceasefire stalls
npr.description: The U.N. peacekeeping mission for Lebanon, known as UNIFIL, said one peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

npr.title: Russia's economic forum opens against backdrop of Ukrainian strikes
npr.description: The St. Petersburg International Economic Forum -- Russia's answer to Davos -- opens under the shadow of Ukrainian drone attacks and growing economic uncertainty.

npr.title: Peru election could add to string of right-wing victories in Latin America
npr.description: Peruvians go to the polls Sunday to elect their next president amid a conservative shift in Latin America. The daughter of a former dictator, a far-right senator, could win.

new-sci.description: A circle running along the 27° east and 153° west meridians divides the globe into two halves with equal reflectivity – and this may have implications for solar geoengineering schemes

new-sci.title: Keto diet shows real promise for anorexia recovery
new-sci.description: Restricting carbohydrates may sound like an unlikely approach to treating anorexia, but following a ketogenic diet was linked to recovery in nearly 75 per cent of people with the eating disorder in a small trial

new-sci.title: Ötzi's frozen remains may harbour metabolically active microbes
new-sci.description: Researchers studying a 5300-year-old mummified man have identified bacteria that lived in his gut when he was alive, as well as cold-tolerant fungi that colonised his body after death

new-sci.title: Why you need to future proof your brain in middle age and how to start
new-sci.description: Ages 40 to 65 see a period of turmoil in the brain that has previously been overlooked. But identifying problems during this time can protect your cognitive health for decades to come

new-sci.title: How the electromagnetic spectrum opened our eyes to the universe
new-sci.description: Our understanding of the electromagnetic spectrum goes back to Isaac Newton, but astronomers are still finding new ways to employ it. Astrophysicist Emma Chapman explores how much these invisible waves can reveal to us about the cosmos – and whether they might show us that we’re not alone

new-sci.title: Hearing loss is bad for the whole body – but new treatments are coming
new-sci.description: From dementia to heart attacks, hearing loss has been linked to a wide range of effects across the body, and the condition is on the rise. Fortunately, we're learning how best to safeguard this crucial sense and how we might be able to reverse the damage

new-sci.title: Hidden store of manganese may have helped Earth get its oxygen
new-sci.description: Computer simulations have uncovered a new manganese compound that could exist deep in Earth’s mantle and may be connected to the process that gave our atmosphere oxygen

new-sci.title: New Scientist recommends Togetherness, a radical new view of life
new-sci.description: An exploration of how biological cooperation underpins all life - and why we’ve overlooked its power until now - makes thrilling reading, finds Penny Sarchet

new-sci.title: A golden age of maths is dawning and mathematicians are freaking out
new-sci.description: Mathematicians are stunned at the progress AI is making in solving advanced problems, leaving some questioning whether there will still be room for humans

phys-org.title: To fight fraud, psychological scientists issue a call to arms
phys-org.description: Journalist Charlotte Cowles received a call about suspicious activity on her Amazon account. A dentist named Daniel answered a call from a number listed as the local police. Mr. Lee, a retired engineer, was told he had to marry his newfound girlfriend so she could receive an inheritance.

phys-org.title: Billions are going into fish passage projects, but planning methods can undercut results
phys-org.description: Fish that split their lives between fresh and salt water often face obstacles getting back and forth. Dams and roads fracture river networks and interfere with traditional migratory routes, sparking concerns about fish health and abundance, as well as biodiversity on a broader scale.

phys-org.title: Buoys track ocean waves across 14,000 km, from storms in Antarctica to ripples in Alaska
phys-org.description: For the first time, mighty ocean waves generated in the Southern Ocean have been accurately measured all the way to the tiny ripples they form on the shores of Alaska. Professor Ian Young, from the University of Melbourne's Department of Infrastructure Engineering, is lead author on a landmark study that analyzed data from 300 drifting ocean buoys to gain a detailed understanding of how storms in Antarctica drive waves all around the globe.

phys-org.title: Costa Rica paid landowners to restore forests and biodiversity—bioacoustics indicate that it worked
phys-org.description: Forest restoration can help fight climate change and restore lost biodiversity, but the satellite-based techniques used to measure successful forest restoration have been less-than-helpful for measuring changes in biodiversity. Instead, a team of researchers listened to the sounds of life in the restored forests. Their new study, published in Global Change Biology, reveals that forest restoration efforts in Costa Rica seem to be working to both regrow forests and restore lost biodiversity.

phys-org.title: Physics-trained digital 'super-brain' speeds nanophotonic design
phys-org.description: Studying physics can be very useful—even when it comes to machine learning. A digital "super-brain" with built-in knowledge of the fundamental laws of nature can speed up the development of optical components for everything from quantum computers to eyeglasses or camera lenses, according to a new study from Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden.

phys-org.title: What network science can tell us about the 2026 World Cup
phys-org.description: Team Australia kicked it long from the goalkeeper. Switzerland took a slower approach and preferred short passes over long drives. Spain, on the other hand, tended to string the ball with sharp, sideways passes across the field. Those are a few of the takeaways from passing-style graphics that Northeastern University's Network Science Institute developed of the top soccer teams at the FIFA World Cup 2022 that showcased their most distinctive passing clusters.

phys-org.title: DNA repair enzyme uses one-dimensional sliding to detect key sites, researchers reveal
phys-org.description: DNA is the blueprint of the human body. However, tens of thousands of DNA lesions occur in our bodies every day. In particular, if "apurinic/apyrimidinic sites" (AP sites, damaged sites where one letter of DNA information has been erased) are not properly repaired, they can lead to cancer and aging.

phys-org.title: 'Out-of-place' rocks reveal how a young ocean formed
phys-org.description: Deep below the Tyrrhenian Sea offshore Italy, scientists drilled into what they thought would be dark mantle rock—and found pieces of granite that seemingly had no business being there. Those unexpected intrusions turned out to offer a rare glimpse of how a massive fault rapidly pulled deep Earth rocks toward the surface during the opening of a young ocean basin.

phys-org.title: Black suburbanization is reshaping American neighborhoods, study finds
phys-org.description: In 1970, nearly half of all Black individuals in the U.S. resided in a large city. Over the past 50 years, that number has fallen to merely 25%, while the share living in the suburbs of large cities rose from 16% to 36%.This demographic shift is as large as the post-World War II wave of the Great Migration, according to economists Evan Mast of the University of Notre Dame and Alexander Bartik of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.

phys-org.title: Jupiter bow shock reveals electrons accelerating to relativistic speeds
phys-org.description: Electrons around Jupiter have been caught in the process of being accelerated, revealing a potentially unified mechanism for particle acceleration. The findings, published in Nature, may help constrain how energetic particles are produced throughout the universe.

phys-org.title: Understanding Earth's hidden east-west symmetry could improve climate models
phys-org.description: Earth is divided into two halves: the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Both reflect equal amounts of sunlight (albedo) even though they have different landmasses and weather patterns, especially cloud distribution. Why this is so is an ongoing mystery waiting to be solved.

phys-org.title: Home-sorted recycling produces higher-quality plastic bales with fewer contaminants, finds study
phys-org.description: The quality of recycled plastic tends to be higher when the waste is pre-sorted by households compared with plastics recovered from mixed waste at a recycling facility in the Netherlands, research in Nature suggests. While mixed waste (not pre-sorted) collections may increase overall recycling volumes, this comes at the cost of reduced quality of the recycled product. The findings highlight the need to improve recycling collection and sorting systems.

phys-org.title: Can fighting via text be good for a relationship?
phys-org.description: Today, many of our social interactions are routed through technology: text messages, video calls, voice messages, emails and instant messaging apps. In romantic relationships, couples often use these methods to deal with conflicts.

phys-org.title: How tuning atomic order and surface chemistry can shape MXenes
phys-org.description: Scientists at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory are helping show what it means to design a material almost atom-by-atom. In two publications, scientists show they can carefully choose the types of atoms in a material, where those atoms sit and what is attached to the surfaces of its atom-thin layers.

phys-org.title: Young caregivers twice as likely to be persistently out of work or education, UK research shows
phys-org.description: New data reveals that young people with caregiving responsibilities are more than twice as likely as their peers to be persistently not in employment, education, or training (NEET) for a period of two years or more. The research, published by City St George's, Carers Trust and University College London, comes just days after the release of the Milburn report into youth unemployment, which identified young caregivers as one of the most "at risk" yet "least visible" groups vulnerable to NEET

phys-org.title: Not too sunny, not too shady, just right for Japanese macaques
phys-org.description: As climate change alters the temperatures of animal habitats, it seems natural that endotherms, warm-blooded animals, would prefer to hang out in the shade during hot weather. The use of microhabitats in the sun and shade is an important thermoregulatory behavior that has been reported across a wide range of animal species, and researchers are becoming increasingly interested in how animals—especially those with long lifespans—flexibly cope with thermal stress.

phys-org.title: DigMethpy: An AI-driven platform for accelerating methane pyrolysis catalyst discovery
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a new artificial intelligence-powered platform that could significantly speed up the discovery of catalysts for methane pyrolysis, a promising technology for producing hydrogen with lower carbon emissions.

phys-org.title: D&D-seq maps DNA-protein interactions in single cells with multi-omics compatibility
phys-org.description: A new technology allows scientists to map, in single cells, the DNA binding sites of transcription factors and other regulatory proteins that control gene activity, according to a study led by investigators at Weill Cornell Medicine and the New York Genome Center. With key advantages over methods currently in use, the technology is expected to be a powerful addition to biologists' toolkit for studying cells in health and disease.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms.
